description: Emergency Mode (patient view). New FastAPI endpoint returns the nearest ER from ml/data/ma_hospitals.csv (rows where emergency_dept=='Yes') using the EXISTING haversine_miles helper, with NO insurance filter (EMTALA / No Surprises Act, decision #14). A new EmergencyTab in the patient phone shows the nearest ER, its straight-line distance, a big keyboard-accessible 'Call 911' tel: button, and the exact reassurance line. Patient location comes from api.patientState(1).patient.lat/lng, labeled on screen as a demo value. Independent of FEAT-002 except both add a tab to PatientPortal.jsx; FEAT-001 introduces the tab bar, FEAT-002 adds its tab to it.
steps: Create backend/app/api/emergency.py: define `router = APIRouter(prefix="/emergency", tags=["emergency"])` and a GET route '/nearest-er' taking query params lat: float and lon: float (NO insurance param). Load the CSV at app.core.config.REPO_ROOT / 'ml' / 'data' / 'ma_hospitals.csv' with the stdlib csv.DictReader; keep only rows where row['emergency_dept'] == 'Yes'; compute distance for each with `from app.services.matching import haversine_miles` as haversine_miles(lat, lon, float(row['lat']), float(row['lon'])); sort ascending by distance. Return {'query': {'lat': lat, 'lon': lon}, 'nearest': <er>, 'top3': [<er>...]} where each <er> is {name, municipality, county, lat, lon, distance_miles} and distance_miles is round(d, 1). Wrap the file read + computation in a helper run via asyncio.to_thread, matching metrics.py/patients.py style.

Register the router in backend/app/main.py: add `emergency` to the `from app.api import appointments, demo, metrics, patients, slots, ws` import line, and add `emergency.router` to the `for r in (appointments.router, slots.router, patients.router, metrics.router, demo.router):` tuple so it gets prefix='/api'. Keep it alphabetical-ish / consistent; do not alter the ws.router line.

Create backend/tests/test_emergency.py using the existing `client` fixture (see backend/tests/conftest.py). Assert: GET /api/emergency/nearest-er?lat=42.30&lon=-71.07 returns 200; response['nearest'] has keys name, municipality, county, lat, lon, distance_miles; distance_miles is a float >= 0; top3 has length <= 3 and is sorted ascending by distance_miles; querying a far-away coordinate (e.g. lat=42.10&lon=-73.20 western MA) yields a DIFFERENT nearest name than the Boston query; and an extra &insurance=NO_INSURANCE query param does not change the result and does not error (proves no insurance filter).

Add the client function in frontend/src/services/api.js: inside the exported `api` object add `nearestEr: (lat, lon) => request(`/emergency/nearest-er?lat=${lat}&lon=${lon}`),` following the existing request() pattern. Additive single line.

Create frontend/src/components/EmergencyTab.jsx. Props: { lat, lng }. Use useState + useEffect to call api.nearestEr(lat, lon) on mount (and a 'Find nearest ER' retry button). Render a prominent heading, the nearest ER (name, municipality, distance in miles labeled 'straight-line / approximate'), a big button `Call 911`, and the EXACT line `ERs must treat you regardless of insurance. You won't be denied emergency care.`. Show a visible label that the location is a demo value. Include NO insurance UI. Ensure large text, high contrast (reuse --text/--card tokens), keyboard focus, and aria labels on the ER info. Handle loading and error states with text (not color alone).

Edit frontend/src/screens/PatientPortal.jsx to introduce the tab bar (additive): add `import EmergencyTab from '../components/EmergencyTab'`; add `const [tab, setTab] = useState('standby')`; wrap the EXISTING pp-body content in a `{tab === 'standby' && ( ... )}` branch WITHOUT changing its offer/socket logic; add a `<div className="tabs" role="tablist">` (same classes as ClinicPortal.jsx) inside the phone with buttons for Standby and Emergency (Coverage button is added by FEAT-002); render `{tab === 'emergency' && <EmergencyTab lat={p.lat} lng={p.lng} />}`. Do not modify connectSocket/refresh/accept/decline logic.

Optional: add minimal additive CSS in frontend/src/styles.css for .call-911 (large padding, high-contrast background e.g. --bad or a red token already present, white text, min touch target ~48px, visible :focus outline). Reuse existing tokens; do not restyle existing classes.
acceptance_criteria: `backend\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q` (from backend/) passes, including the new backend/tests/test_emergency.py.

GET /api/emergency/nearest-er?lat=42.30&lon=-71.07 returns a nearest ER with the documented keys and a numeric distance_miles, and the endpoint accepts NO insurance filter (an insurance query param is ignored).
The endpoint computes distance via app.services.matching.haversine_miles (imported, not reimplemented) and only considers rows where emergency_dept == 'Yes'.
`npm run build` (from frontend/) succeeds with the new EmergencyTab wired into PatientPortal.jsx.

The Emergency UI shows the nearest ER + distance, a tel:911 Call 911 button with an aria-label, the exact reassurance line verbatim, a demo-location label, and NO insurance input; it is keyboard operable with large, high-contrast text.
verification: From backend/: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q` — all tests pass.
From frontend/: `npm run build` — build succeeds, no errors.

From backend/: start `.venv\Scripts\uvicorn.exe app.main:app --port 8000`, then `curl "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/emergency/nearest-er?lat=42.30&lon=-71.07"` returns JSON with nearest + distance_miles; stop the server afterward.
findings:
Implemented. Backend: backend/app/api/emergency.py exposes GET /api/emergency/nearest-er?lat=&lon= (no insurance param); loads ml/data/ma_hospitals.csv via REPO_ROOT, keeps rows where emergency_dept=='Yes', distances via the existing app.services.matching.haversine_miles, CSV read+compute wrapped in asyncio.to_thread. Returns {query:{lat,lon}, nearest:, top3:[...]} with er={name,municipality,county,lat,lon,distance_miles(rounded 1dp)}. Router registered in main.py (added to the import line and the for-r include tuple with prefix=/api; ws.router untouched). Tests: backend/tests/test_emergency.py (3 tests) all green. Frontend: api.js has nearestEr(lat,lon). New EmergencyTab.jsx (props lat,lng) calls api.nearestEr on mount + 'Find nearest ER' retry; shows nearest ER name/municipality/county, distance labeled 'straight-line / approximate', a big Call 911, the EXACT line "ERs must treat you regardless of insurance. You won't be denied emergency care.", a demo-location note, loading/error states as text (role=alert). No insurance UI. CSS .call-911 added in styles.css (var(--bad) bg, white text, 48px+ touch target, visible :focus-visible outline) reusing existing tokens. FEAT-001 introduced the tab bar in PatientPortal.jsx: const [tab,setTab]=useState('standby'); a
(same classes as ClinicPortal) with Standby + Emergency buttons (role=tab, aria-selected). Existing pp-body offer/socket logic is unchanged, now wrapped in {tab==='standby' && (...)}. Emergency renders {tab==='emergency' && } inside a pp-body wrapper. NOTE FOR FEAT-002: the tab bar now exists in PatientPortal.jsx. Add the Coverage tab by (1) adding a third to the existing .tabs div, and (2) adding {tab==='coverage' && (
)} alongside the emergency branch. Do not touch the standby branch.
